sourcedFrom: Beretta 92X PERFORMANCE User Manual — C6C587 005 - P022786 002 (form code printed in the running header) (UNDATED — Beretta prints a form code rather than a year in these books)

steps.title: Unloaded, glasses on, work over a table
steps.action: Prove it empty before the latch is touched. Beretta asks for eye protection here and for a table under the work — the recoil spring and guide are why, and on a Performance they are heavier than a standard 92's.
steps.aside: CAUTION: It is advisable to carry out the field stripping and the assembly operations over a table to catch components should they drop.
steps.quote: WARNING: Make sure the pistol is unloaded. If not, unload it following the procedure “UNLOADING” on page 17.
steps.cite: Beretta 92X PERFORMANCE User Manual — C6C587 005 - P022786 002 (form code printed in the running header) — FIELD STRIPPING, printed p.31-32

steps.title: Magazine out, disassembly latch 90° down
steps.action: Drop the magazine, hold the pistol in your right hand, press the disassembly latch release button on the RIGHT side with your left forefinger and rotate the latch on the LEFT side clockwise about 90 degrees downward with your thumb. Both sides at once — that is the part people fight.
steps.quote: Hold the pistol in the right hand and with left forefinger press the disassembly latch release button which protrudes from the right side of the pistol. While it is held in, rotate the disassembly latch on the left side of the frame with the thumb clockwise approx. 90° downward.
steps.cite: Beretta 92X PERFORMANCE User Manual — C6C587 005 - P022786 002 (form code printed in the running header) — FIELD STRIPPING, printed p.31-32

steps.title: Slide-barrel assembly forward off the frame
steps.action: Run the slide-barrel assembly straight forward off the frame. Locking block, recoil spring and spring guide come with it.
steps.quote: Pull the slide-barrel assembly with locking block, recoil spring and spring guide forwards
steps.cite: Beretta 92X PERFORMANCE User Manual — C6C587 005 - P022786 002 (form code printed in the running header) — FIELD STRIPPING, printed p.31-32

steps.title: ⛔ Spring and guide are under tension
steps.action: Press the recoil spring and spring guide slightly, then lift the guide and let the spring stretch out SLOWLY. A Performance's spring is stiff; released carelessly it goes across the room.
steps.quote: WARNING: Spring and spring guide are under tension. Lift spring guide and recoil spring, letting the latter stretch slowly.
steps.cite: Beretta 92X PERFORMANCE User Manual — C6C587 005 - P022786 002 (form code printed in the running header) — FIELD STRIPPING, printed p.31-32

steps.title: Locking block plunger, then the barrel — strip complete
steps.action: Depress the locking block plunger and lift the barrel's locking assembly out of the slide. That is the end of the published strip; Beretta stops the owner here in as many words.
steps.aside: CAUTION: No further disassembly is recommended unless done by a competent gunsmith.
steps.quote: Depress the locking block plunger. Remove the barrel’s locking assembly from the slide
steps.cite: Beretta 92X PERFORMANCE User Manual — C6C587 005 - P022786 002 (form code printed in the running header) — FIELD STRIPPING, printed p.31-32

steps.title: Bore from the chamber end, never with the gun together
steps.action: Brush from the chamber end and scrub chamber and bore, solvent first if it needs it, then patches until one emerges clean. The barrel is out of the pistol for this — Beretta is explicit that it is not cleaned assembled.
steps.aside: WARNING: Do not clean the barrel with the pistol assembled.
steps.quote: Insert the brush into the barrel from the chamber and scrub the chamber and bore thoroughly. If necessary, first clean the bore with a gun solvent.
steps.cite: Beretta 92X PERFORMANCE User Manual — C6C587 005 - P022786 002 (form code printed in the running header) — MAINTENANCE, printed p.41

steps.title: ⛔ Hammer and sear are DLC — no abrasive, no polish, no file
steps.action: If you go anywhere near the hammer or sear with anything abrasive on a Performance you will destroy the coating that makes the trigger what it is. Beretta prints the warning in this book and in no other in the drop. Oil-soaked patch only.
steps.quote: CAUTION: Hammer and sear finishing is DLC (Diamond Like Carbon). Use of abrasive paper or polish, not to mention filing, will remove the coating.
steps.cite: Beretta 92X PERFORMANCE User Manual — C6C587 005 - P022786 002 (form code printed in the running header) — MAINTENANCE, printed p.42

steps.title: Frame, latch and the trigger-mechanism levers
steps.action: Clean everywhere gunpowder residue and dirt have collected, wipe the outer frame surfaces, then lightly oil the rails and the moving parts by name — disassembly latch, magazine release, slide stop, trigger, hammer, safeties and the trigger-mechanism levers.
steps.aside: CAUTION: Do not apply excess oil. Accumulation of oil attracts dirt and dust, which can interfere with the functioning and reliability of the firearm.
steps.quote: Wipe outer frame surfaces clean and lightly lubricate the rails and moving parts. Lightly oil the disassembly latch, magazine release button, slide stop, trigger, hammer, safeties and the trigger mechanism levers.
steps.cite: Beretta 92X PERFORMANCE User Manual — C6C587 005 - P022786 002 (form code printed in the running header) — MAINTENANCE, printed p.42

steps.title: Magazine dry inside — no lubricant left in the box
steps.action: The follower must slide down freely under thumb pressure. Lightly oil the internal walls only if it needs it, then run a DRY patch through: Beretta does not want lubricant left inside the magazine box, because it collects the dust that stops the follower.
steps.quote: Run a dry patch through the box. Do not leave lubricant inside the magazine box.
steps.cite: Beretta 92X PERFORMANCE User Manual — C6C587 005 - P022786 002 (form code printed in the running header) — MAINTENANCE, printed p.42

deepAbsentReason: Beretta stops the owner at the field strip on this pistol and prints it on the page: "No further disassembly is recommended unless done by a competent gunsmith." There is no deeper published procedure to author, and a manufacturer's DON'T outranks every other tier, so nothing is borrowed from elsewhere to fill it.

cleaning.name: BARREL
tasks: Brush in from the CHAMBER end and all the way through before pulling back
Solvent first if it needs it, then patches until one comes out clean
⛔ Never clean the barrel with the pistol assembled
Light oil on the whole barrel before it goes back

cleaning.name: SLIDE & BREECH FACE
tasks: Cloth or nylon brush on the breech face, extractor, rails and locking shoulders
Dry the slide surfaces, then lightly oil the guides

cleaning.name: RECOIL SPRING ASSEMBLY
tasks: Light gun oil on the spring guide assembly
Nylon brush first if it is heavily fouled — never a steel one

cleaning.name: FRAME & MAGAZINE
tasks: Fouling off the frame rails and the magazine well
Magazine lips and follower cleaned, then wiped with a lightly oiled rag
⛔ Never spray or apply oil to cartridges

reassembly: Barrel into the slide first, muzzle end through the front, rear lowered into place.
Recoil spring and guide assembly seated in its recess against the barrel lug.
Slide assembly onto the frame rails and pushed rearward until it locks.
⛔ Confirm the disassembly latch is back in the LOCKED position before releasing a slide under spring pressure.
Cycle the slide several times, decock if the model has a decocker, then function check.
fncheck: Reassembled and unloaded, rack the slide several times and confirm it goes fully into battery and that the disassembly latch has returned to its locked position — Beretta warns that a slide released under spring pressure with the latch unlocked can launch off the frame. Check the safety or decocker works as the manual describes, then dry-cycle once more before loading.
